summary: Root-caused Orb.cs's TotalTrades=0 bug (task t-b2d143): NT8's Managed order approach silently ignores both opposite-direction stop entries submitted together (confirmed via a screenshot of NT8's Output panel showing 'Internal Order Handling Rules that Reduce Unwanted Positions'), which is exactly ORB's straddle-OCO entry pattern. Rewrote Orb.cs to use NT8's documented fix - the Unmanaged order approach with OCO ids linking the entry pair and the stop/target pair - and fixed a second bug (leftover Managed-only properties conflicting with IsUnmanaged=true, which was hanging test jobs with no result written). Committed and pushed both the code fix (9459cfb) and a docs update (091384b). Also proved out and documented a headless NT8 recompile workflow via Windows UI Automation (PowerShell driving the already-open NinjaScript Editor window: focus + send F5), including two real gotchas - stale editor tab buffers not reloading from disk, and no UI-Automation-readable output/error surface (screenshots are the only way to read Print()/compile errors back). Full details in docs/research/nt8-automation-notes.md.
next_steps: 1. Recompile the just-pushed fix using the now-documented ritual in docs/research/nt8-automation-notes.md (close+reopen the Orb.cs tab from the NinjaScript Explorer tree to force a disk reload, then F5) - can be done by hand or via the PowerShell UI Automation approach proven this session. 2. Drop a fresh small test job (1-week range) and check ninjascript/results/testN.result.txt - confirms whether the hang is fixed and whether TotalTrades>0 now (the actual proof the Unmanaged rewrite works). 3. See task t-b2d143 for full history/details. 4. Once Orb.cs produces sane trade counts, run the prop_sim/registry comparison this whole task was originally for. 5. Consider building tools/nt8_recompile.ps1 to consolidate the manual recompile ritual into one script, per the notes doc.
questions: The headless-recompile workaround always chooses to discard an editor tab's 'unsaved changes' on the assumption this repo (via deploy.ps1) is the sole source of truth for these files. That's safe today but would silently destroy real work if anyone ever edits directly inside NT8's NinjaScript Editor instead - worth a guardrail if this becomes a standing automated ritual.
